pointers.sentence: So the manager reads each row once and keeps it: lookups "are cached so that subsequent lookups for the same model don't hit the database", says the docstring of `ContentTypeManager.get_for_model` (`django/contrib/contenttypes/models.py:ContentTypeManager`).
`unique_together` makes the pair unique, and the table is `"django_content_type"` (`django/contrib/contenttypes/models.py:ContentType`).

A content type's key "isn't easy to predict", the documentation says, since it depends on how and when migrate ran; data serialized with natural keys names a content type by its pair instead (`docs/topics/serialization.txt`).

The base manager is a plain `Manager` unless the model's options name another (`django/db/models/options.py:Options.base_manager`) ([Managers](../models/managers.md#the-default-manager-and-the-base-manager)): Veteran's manager keeps the sailors who signed on before 2020, yet Veteran's own content type found Ada, who signed on in the run, with one query of `"crew_sailor"` and no condition on the date (`django/contrib/contenttypes/models.py:ContentType.get_object_for_this_type`).

The base manager is a plain `Manager` unless the model's options name another (`django/db/models/options.py:Options.base_manager`) ([Managers](../models/managers.md#the-default-manager-and-the-base-manager)): Veteran's manager keeps the sailors who signed on before 2020, yet Veteran's own content type found Ada, who signed on in the run, with one query of `"crew_sailor"` and no condition on the date (`django/contrib/contenttypes/models.py:ContentType.get_object_for_this_type`).

Reading one note's object, the generic foreign key calls `get_object_for_this_type` (`django/contrib/contenttypes/fields.py:GenericForeignKeyDescriptor.fetch_one`), so through a stale content type it raised the same error.
The alias is the manager's `BaseManager.db`: the one `BaseManager.db_manager` set, or else the router's `db_for_read` for `ContentType` (`django/db/models/manager.py:BaseManager.db`).

`ContentType.objects` is a copy of the manager the class declares, made by its options (`django/db/models/options.py:Options.managers`), and `db_manager` makes another; the copies are shallow, so all of them share the one dictionary.

`ContentTypeManager._get_opts` takes the options of its concrete model, or of the model itself with `for_concrete_model=False`, and the cache is read by the pair (`django/contrib/contenttypes/models.py:ContentTypeManager.get_for_model`).

The admin passes `for_concrete_model=False`, so a change made through a proxy's admin is logged under the proxy (`django/contrib/admin/models.py:LogEntryManager.log_actions`), and a proxy's permissions are made with its own content type ([Making the permissions: `create_permissions`](../auth/creating-permissions.md)).

It answers what it can from the cache, reads the rest in one query, an OR of one condition for each application label, and makes each row still missing with `QuerySet.create`, one at a time (`django/contrib/contenttypes/models.py:ContentTypeManager.get_for_models`).

The generic foreign key finds a note's content type with `get_for_id`; a deserializer finds one by its natural key with `get_by_natural_key`, as `PermissionManager.get_by_natural_key` does for a permission's (`django/contrib/auth/models.py:PermissionManager.get_by_natural_key`).

Since `ContentTypeManager.use_in_migrations` is true, the historical `ContentType` a migration is given has the manager too, but a new instance of it, with a dictionary of its own (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ModelState.construct_managers`).

`create_contenttypes` ([Making content types: `create_contenttypes` and `RenameContentType`](making-content-types.md)) clears that of the `ContentType` in the registry it is given, before it reads the rows: flush gives it the project's own, and a flush emptied the process's cache; migrate gives it the historical registry, and a migrate called in the run left the process's cache as it was (`django/contrib/contenttypes/management/__init__.py:create_contenttypes`).
Django's documentation has a test call `clear_cache` in its set-up and again in a cleanup (`docs/ref/contrib/contenttypes.txt`).
